title: 10.8.0: Exercises
originalText:
Use the Pythagorean theorem to answer the following exercises. Let \(a\) and \(b\) represent two legs of a right triangle, and let \(c\) represent the hypotenuse. Find the lengths of the missing sides.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{1}\)

[Figure: A right triangle. The legs are labeled a equals 7 and b. The hypotenuse is labeled c equals 25.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{2}\)

[Figure: A right triangle. The legs are labeled a equals 8 and b equals 15. The hypotenuse is labeled c.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{3}\)

If \(b = 25\) and \(c = 65{\text{ ft}}\), find \(a\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{4}\)

If \(a = 18{\text{ ft}}\) and \(c = 30{\text{ ft}}\), find \(b\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{5}\)

If \(b = 12{\text{ cm}}\) and \(c = 15{\text{ cm}}\), find \(a\).

Refer to the \({30^ \circ} {\text{-}} {60^ \circ } {\text{-}} {90^ \circ }\) triangle shown for the following exercises.

[Figure: A right triangle. The legs are labeled a and b. The hypotenuse is labeled c. The angles at the top, bottom-left, and bottom-right are labeled 60 degrees, 90 degrees, and 30 degrees.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{6}\)

If \(b = 10\), find \(c\) and \(a\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{7}\)

If \(a = 2\sqrt 3{\text{ ft}}\), find \(b\) and \(c\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{8}\)

If \(b = 7{\text{ cm}}\), find \(a\) and \(c\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{9}\)

If \(c = \sqrt 3 \), find \(a\) and \(b\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{10}\)

If \(c = 8\sqrt 3 \), find \(a\) and \(b\)

Refer to the \({45^ \circ }{\text{-}}{45^ \circ }{\text{-}}{90^ \circ }\) triangle shown in the following exercises.

[Figure: A right triangle. The legs are labeled a and b. The hypotenuse is labeled c. The angles at the top, bottom-left, and bottom-right are labeled 90 degrees, 45 degrees, and 45 degrees.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{11}\)

If \(a = 15{\text{ cm}}\), find \(b\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{12}\)

If \(a = 3\sqrt {2}{\text{ ft}}\), find \(a\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{13}\)

If \(a = 4\sqrt 5{\text{ cm}}\), find \(b\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{14}\)

If \(a = 10{\text{ ft}}\), find \(b\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{15}\)

If \(b = \frac

Exercise \(\PageIndex{16}\)

In the provided figure given \(\alpha = {10^ \circ }\), find the unknown sides and angles.

[Figure: A right triangle. The legs are labeled a equals 11 and b. The angles at the top, bottom-left, and bottom-right are labeled beta, 90 degrees, and alpha.]

Evaluate the expressions in the following exercises.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{17}\)

\({\sin ^{ - 1}}\left( {\frac{2}{5}} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{18}\)

\({\tan ^{ - 1}}(5.68)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{19}\)

\({\cos ^{ - 1}}\left( {\frac{1}{9}} \right)\)

Exercise \(\PageIndex{20}\)

Use the figure shown to solve for all missing sides and angles given \(a = 6,\,b = 8\).

[Figure: A right triangle. The legs are labeled b and a. The hypotenuse is labeled c. The angles at the top, bottom-left, and bottom-right are labeled beta, alpha, and 90 degrees.]

Exercise \(\PageIndex{21}\)

Use the figure shown to solve for all missing sides and angles given \(\alpha = {16^ \circ },\,c = 20\).

[Figure: A right triangle. The legs are labeled b and a. The hypotenuse is labeled 20. The angles at the top, bottom-left, and bottom-right are labeled beta, 90 degrees, and 16 degrees.]
